newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US T-BONDS' BOUNCE STILL SEEN TENTATIVE.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US T-BONDS' BOUNCE STILL SEEN TENTATIVE.

text.p: A mild rebound in U.S. Treasury bond futures this week after last week's freefall still looks frail and the upside potential is likely to be limited near term, technical analysts said.

Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group, said the technical picture was so fragile at the moment that some of the economic data due out later in the week could easily change the outlook.
"We have three numbers coming out in the next two days," he said, referring to Wednesday's July retail sales and producer price index and Thursday's consumer price index.

Still, September T-bond futures could extend their gains toward 114-2/32 if the numbers are tame, even if the bounce was of a corrective nature, he noted. A descending trendline from the August 1 high of 116-31/32 and last week's 115-6/32 came in at that level.
The September contract was up 14/32 at 113-6/32 in mid-morning business.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, said the 60-minute and 100-minute stochastics had made clear bullish divergences and upcrossed in the past few days, boding well for the coming few sessions.
He added that there was a 10-tick gap below 114-3/32 on the 100-minute chart for daytime pit sessions, and the market was likely to fill it in the coming week or so.
"The hondo (100-minute) never leaves a gap unfilled," he said. "So we've got those two bullish divergences plus the gap working for us."

With the daily stochastic about to reach a bottom, the September contract could test the mid-114 area, Grauer predicted. However, the weekly stochastic, which "keeled over and died" last week, would dampen upward momentum during its down cycle, which typically lasted about 12 weeks, he added.
Most analysts did not expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at the August 19 Federal Open Market Committee meeting and expected the market to eventually return to its underlying uptrend.
Both Crosson and Grauer saw little downside potential and pegged the worst-case projection in the mid-110 area.
Crosson said that was the measured target for last week's break from the April-August uptrend channel, while Grauer said the level represented a 50-percent retracement of that four-month rally.
Crosson added that the Commodity Research Bureau index .CRB, which had risen sharply in late July, appeared to be topping out and offered some relief.
Grauer said the monthly stochastic, which had upturned earlier in the year and firmly upcrossed in May, was only halfway through its bullish cycle and was likely to continue pressing higher.
"The second half of cycle, when we get there, is much stronger than the first," he said.
